lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Unit performance task: recovering when a deadline is missed

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic recovering when a deadline is missed task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner updates their real tracker from day 1 with current status, runs it against three additional provided simulated deadlines to stress-test the system across a fuller cycle, then works through a scenario where one deadline (real or simulated) was missed or nearly missed, drafting a specific recovery plan that a guardian reviews and discusses with them.
safetyNotes: The three additional stress-test deadlines are provided and simulated so the exercise works the same way regardless of how many real deadlines the learner currently has active.
The guardian review focuses on the tracker and recovery plan as documents; no real account, application, or contact with an unfamiliar adult is required to complete this lesson.

simulationAlternative.description: If the learner has no real deadlines currently active to update, the tracker portion is completed entirely using a provided fully-simulated four-deadline set instead, and the recovery-plan scenario is built around one of those simulated deadlines.

materials: learner-local: the learner's own tracker from day 1 of this unit
learner-local: the three provided simulated deadlines

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Looking back across this whole unit, what specific habit from your tracker system would have caught this problem earlier, before it became a three-day emergency?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Tracker integration: Real items are updated with current status and simulated deadlines are recorded in the same format and detail. | Recovery plan concreteness: Recovery plan includes an ordered list of specific actions and a realistic first-contact message. | System-level transfer: Reflection names one specific tracker habit or feature that would have caught the problem earlier. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a permanent 'early warning' column or rule to their real tracker (for example, flagging any document still not started with fewer than 14 days left) designed specifically to prevent the kind of near-miss they just worked through, and explain in a sentence how it would have caught this scenario earlier.

resources.title: recovering when a deadline is missed worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner updates their real tracker from day 1 with current status, runs it against three additional provided simulated deadlines to stress-test the system across a fuller cycle, then works through a scenario where one deadline (real or simulated) was missed or nearly missed, drafting a specific recovery plan that a guardian reviews and discusses with them.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact recovering when a deadline is missed decision or action.
Model move 2: Update your tracker from day 1 with the current real status of each item, then add the three provided simulated deadlines to it in the same format.

Model move 3: Read the provided scenario: one item on your combined tracker (you choose which, real or simulated) has just been discovered to be either missed entirely or dangerously close to missed, three days before its deadline, with one required document still not ready.

resources.title: recovering when a deadline is missed action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for recovering when a deadline is missed.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.

resources.title: recovering when a deadline is missed coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner updates their real tracker from day 1 with current status, runs it against three additional provided simulated deadlines to stress-test the system across a fuller cycle, then works through a scenario where one deadline (real or simulated) was missed or nearly missed, drafting a specific recovery plan that a guardian reviews and discusses with them.
Coach direction: Update your tracker from day 1 with the current real status of each item, then add the three provided simulated deadlines to it in the same format.
Learner prompt: Show your updated tracker with current statuses for your real items, plus the three simulated deadlines added in the same format.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: recovering when a deadline is missed complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read the provided scenario: one item on your combined tracker (you choose which, real or simulated) has just been discovered to be either missed entirely or dangerously close to missed, three days before its deadline, with one required document still not ready.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Which item did you choose, and what specifically went wrong (what was missed and why, based on your tracker)?
Response 2 (t2-p2): Write a specific recovery plan: what you would do first, in what order, including who you would contact and what you would say to explain the situation and ask for what you need.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My recovery plan includes a realistic first message to whoever needs to be contacted (an admissions office, a reference-writer, a program coordinator), not just a list of steps.

Equal-access rule: If the learner has no real deadlines currently active to update, the tracker portion is completed entirely using a provided fully-simulated four-deadline set instead, and the recovery-plan scenario is built around one of those simulated deadlines.

resources.title: recovering when a deadline is missed minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Looking back across this whole unit, what specific habit from your tracker system would have caught this problem earlier, before it became a three-day emergency?

Success checks: Tracker integration: Real items are updated with current status and simulated deadlines are recorded in the same format and detail. | Recovery plan concreteness: Recovery plan includes an ordered list of specific actions and a realistic first-contact message. | System-level transfer: Reflection names one specific tracker habit or feature that would have caught the problem earlier.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: recovering when a deadline is missed supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional recovering when a deadline is missed condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Tracker integration: Real items are updated with current status and simulated deadlines are recorded in the same format and detail. | Recovery plan concreteness: Recovery plan includes an ordered list of specific actions and a realistic first-contact message. | System-level transfer: Reflection names one specific tracker habit or feature that would have caught the problem earlier..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
